members.name: p4g_v5_a
members.instructions: You see a charity-donation chat in which a persuader tries to get the persuadee to donate their task payment to Save the Children, then one persuader message. Which persuasion strategy or dialogue act does that LAST persuader message (after 'Persuader message to tag') use? Judge only that message, using the chat only as context (e.g. what it replies to). Note: the chat lines may be out of order.

criteria.greeting_hello: Opening greeting or pleasantries: 'Hi', 'Hello there!', 'How are you today?', 'I'm good, how are you?', 'I am very good.' (answering how they are), 'Nice to meet you'.
criteria.closing_goodbye: Closing / farewell at the end of the chat: 'Have a great day!', 'Take care', 'Hope you enjoy the rest of your day', 'Bye'.
criteria.thank_you: Thanking the persuadee: 'Thank you so much for your donation', 'Thanks for your time', 'Thank you for doing this'.
criteria.praise_persuadee: Compliments the persuadee as a person or their generosity/decision: 'You are a kind person', 'People like you make the world better', 'That's awesome and generous!', and a bare 'Great!/Awesome!/That's great!' said right after the persuadee commits or agrees to donate.
criteria.acknowledge: A brief reaction to what the persuadee just said (not right after a donation commitment): agreeing, confirming or empathising ('Absolutely.', 'Yes they do.', 'I agree', 'Me too', 'I definitely understand', 'Same here!', 'That's great to hear', 'Wow', 'That's really good news', 'Ok, that makes sense', 'I know').
criteria.filler_or_short_answer: A flat, noncommittal filler with no strategy: 'Ok...', 'Fine...', 'yeah..', 'Yes, indeed.', or a short 'Yes.'/'I have.'/'I do' answering a question the persuadee asked.
criteria.confirm_amount_or_ask_more: Confirms the amount the persuadee said ('So you are donating $10, right?', 'Just to be sure you want to donate 1 dollar?') or asks them to donate more than they offered ('Would you be willing to donate a bit more?').
criteria.task_meta_or_misc: Remarks about the chat/HIT/task itself ('we need 10 chats to complete this hit'), typo corrections ('Sorry, typo!', 'sorry, I meant...'), non-English messages, arguing with or insulting the persuadee, talk about other charities (not Save the Children) or the persuader's own volunteering/charity activities that are not about donating money ('I'm getting ready to volunteer for my favorite charity!'), or anything fitting no other option.
criteria.off_task_chat: Small talk unrelated to the charity or donating: the persuader's location, travel, hobbies, celebrities, weather, local food, jobs, etc. ('I'm back in the UK now', 'North Carolina is nice', 'John Cena is amazing').
criteria.propose_donation: Directly asks or urges the persuadee to donate, as a yes/no ask (a yes/no ask, not a 'how much' question or a suggestion of specific amounts): 'Would you be willing to donate some of your task payment?', 'Would you like to help by donating?', 'We should donate to them!', 'Could I interest you in that?'.
criteria.ask_amount: Asks HOW MUCH the persuadee wants to donate (any 'how much...' question, even 'how much would you be willing to donate?'), or suggests specific amounts for them to pick ('May I suggest $.50 or even $1 if you are able?', 'could you afford maybe fifteen cents?', 'Half of 1 dollar?'): 'How much would you like to donate?', 'How much of the money you earn from this task would you be willing to donate?', 'What amount would you feel comfortable donating?', 'What do you think you will be donating?'.
criteria.donation_procedure: Explains the donation procedure or answers the persuadee's questions about how donating works: payment is deducted from task payment, the research team collects and sends it to Save the Children, the allowed range ($0 to full payment), any amount is acceptable, how/where to give, it is tax deductible, a matching partnership.
criteria.small_amount_helps: Starts small: stresses that even a tiny amount helps or asks for a small first step ('Every little bit helps', 'Even 10 cents makes a difference', 'sometimes even a small help is a lot', 'they only ask for a small amount we might spend on coffee or snacks' (the point must be how SMALL the requested amount is), 'Even the smallest donation would make a difference', 'could you afford maybe fifteen cents?', 'just a few cents').
criteria.org_info: Any statement about Save the Children itself: introducing or naming it, what it does and where it works, its programs, history, founder, finances ('86% goes to program services'), ratings, reputation, praise of the organisation ('it is a trustable fund', 'They are very renowned'), its website or URL, and answers to 'what do they do?'. Also the charity acting on a problem. If a message states such a fact about the organisation and then adds a short question ('Is this something you care about?'), it is still this option.
criteria.children_suffering: Evokes feelings about children's suffering or the persuader's feelings: deaths, war, hunger, poverty ('1,000 children were killed in Syria', 'Some of them have no shoes', 'It makes me so sad', 'That horrifies me!'), the persuader's heartfelt wish to help children ('I want to help all the children in the world'), 'imagine...', guilt, how good the persuadee will feel, 'the children need you'.
criteria.reasoning: Reasoning or argument for donating: donations make a real difference, moral reasoning ('we should all help', 'children are the future', 'everyone deserves a fighting chance'), 'if everyone gave a nickel...', and arguments that we waste money on unnecessary things (candy, snacks, dining out) that could help children instead.
criteria.persuader_donates: The persuader states their own donating behaviour or intention toward Save the Children or this donation (not giving to unrelated causes like animal shelters): 'I will donate $1 as well', 'I donate to them regularly', 'I'll match your donation', 'I gave what was given to me', 'I try to donate annually'.
criteria.story: A narrative about a personal experience or a specific person: the persuader's own experiences, travels or first-hand observations ('I worked in Africa and saw...', 'I volunteer at a food bank', 'When I visited poor countries I saw how much a little donation does') or a story about a child (e.g. the story of Bruce).
criteria.ask_about_org: Asks whether the persuadee knows about or has heard of Save the Children, or what they know/think of the organisation: 'Have you heard of Save the Children?', 'Are you familiar with them?'.
criteria.ask_about_giving: Asks the persuadee's opinions or experiences about donating, charities, volunteering or the children's cause: 'Do you donate to charities?', 'Have you ever donated?', 'What do you think about child abuse?', 'Did you know 16,000 children die each day?', 'Do you have questions?', 'What do you think?'.
criteria.ask_personal: Asks about the persuadee's personal life unrelated to giving: 'Do you have children?', 'Where are you from?', 'How is your life?', 'What is the specialty in your place?'.
